title: Oven cleaning paste
subtitle: A bicarbonate paste applied overnight for baked-on grease
excerpt: Oven cleaning paste is a thick bicarbonate of soda and washing-up liquid paste applied to the interior surfaces of a cool oven and left overnight before wiping away. It loosens baked-on grease and carbon deposits without fumes or caustic chemicals. Mix a fresh batch per clean; one batch covers a standard single oven.
sourceNotes: Bicarbonate of soda oven-cleaning method: Natural Cleaning Solutions by Rachel Ogden (2012) and Go Green by Lisa Benjamin (2018). Bicarbonate of soda (pH ~8.3) loosens baked-on grease by raising the local pH of the carbonised deposits, making them more water-soluble. The overnight dwell time is critical, short-contact applications are significantly less effective on heavily carbonised surfaces. White vinegar spray after wiping neutralises any residual bicarbonate before using the oven.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~300 g of cleaning paste (enough for 1 standard single oven)
recipe.batchNotes: Mix fresh per clean. Do not store the mixed paste.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Apply before bed and wipe clean in the morning.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use immediately. Do not store the mixed paste.

glossaryTerms.definition: Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda), a mild alkaline powder used in cleaning to loosen grease and carbon deposits by raising local pH. Not the same as washing soda (sodium carbonate), which is much more strongly alkaline.

content.text: Make sure the oven is completely cool before starting. Mix the bicarbonate of soda, washing-up liquid, and water to a thick, spreadable paste. Wearing rubber gloves, spread the paste over all the interior surfaces of the oven, the base, sides, back, and inside of the door, avoiding the heating elements and the oven light. The paste will be white; do not worry about even coverage on the first pass. Apply a thicker layer over the most heavily soiled areas.
Close the oven door and leave for eight to twelve hours. Do not use the oven during this time. The longer the dwell time, the more the grease loosens.

Wipe the paste away with a damp cloth, working in sections. The paste will have turned grey or brown where it has absorbed the grease. Stubborn spots may need a second wipe with a damp sponge. Once the bulk of the paste is removed, spray the oven interior lightly with white vinegar, it will foam where residual bicarbonate remains. Wipe again with a damp cloth. Leave the oven door open for 30 minutes before the next use to allow any residual moisture to evaporate.

A single overnight application removes most grease from a regularly maintained oven. If the oven has not been cleaned in a long time, a second application the following night will get the rest. The paste does not damage enamel, glass, or stainless steel surfaces.
